result.summary:
The 45.8s capture (Firefox 132, Windows 10) holds three navigation-like episodes in the same content process. Each is marked by browser-metric:fmp at 4.08s, 18.03s and 28.62s, FirstContentfulPaint at 742–802ms, and the site's own browser-metric:tti at 1.22–1.52s. There are no unload or DocumentLoad markers, and the cost includes dynamic-import module evaluation, which suggests SPA route changes. This is an inference, not confirmed.

In each episode the content main thread is busy for about 4.6–6s (77–84% of samples). The work is diffuse:
- module loading/evaluation and compilation ≈ 25%
- IndexedDB success handlers ≈ 12%
- postMessage handlers ≈ 10%
- GC/CC slices
- rAF callbacks ≈ 7%
- sync WebGL IPC waits ≈ 6–7%

The longest task per episode (423ms, 322ms, 270ms) is page promise-callback JS, with about 27% of it in incremental major-GC slices. Two things are worth an engineer's attention.
1. The JS heap and GC/CC cost grow with every navigation and never return to baseline: post-GC heap 213→325MB, CC visited GC things 100k→729k. Each later episode therefore pays more GC/CC.
2. The main thread blocks in synchronous WebGL IPC. One getError call in each episode, made right after a sprite-sheet texture init, waits 110–125ms.

Even with no navigation in progress (36–45.8s), the main thread stays about 40% busy, mostly in rAF callbacks and GC/CC.
result.hot_path: Content GeckoMain (Isolated Web Content, pid 3608). Promise/AsyncFunctionNext page JS. ScriptLoader::ProcessPendingRequests → ModuleLoaderBase::InstantiateAndEvaluateDynamicImport. BackgroundRequestChild::Recv__delete__ (IndexedDB). PostMessageEvent::Run. Also ClientWebGLContext::GetError/GetLinkResult → PWebGLChild::Send* → MessageChannel::WaitForSyncNotify, and incremental GC/CC slices.
result.recommendation: Capture again with the profiler's 'Native Allocations' or JS allocation tracking and with all GPU-process threads (or the WebGL/Canvas thread) included, across 3+ repeated navigations. That would show whether heap growth (213→325MB) and the long getError waits come from page code or Gecko. Ask the reporter which interval they perceive as slow.

controls.control: the same thread with no navigation running
controls.rationale: The 36-45.8s window, where ScriptLoader and IndexedDB work drop to ~0, against the three post-navigation windows in the same profile. It shows roughly half the main-thread work during an episode is background load (rAF + GC/CC) that is always present, not navigation-specific.

result.headline: Each of the three in-app navigations keeps the content main thread 77–84% busy for about 4.6–6s. The time is spread across page JS (dynamic-import module evaluation, IndexedDB and postMessage handlers), GC/CC whose cost and heap grow with every navigation, and sync WebGL IPC waits. No single Gecko hot path dominates.
key_figures: Per navigation: 1769–2115 of 2287–2927 main-thread samples active (~2ms/sample); ScriptLoader 477–543, IndexedDB 210–239, PostMessage 190–209
Post-GC heap grows 213MB→229→245→284→288→325MB across the capture; GCMajor total_time grows 79ms→362ms, CC from 134ms to 639ms
Main thread spends 739 samples blocked in sync WebGL IPC (MessageChannel::WaitForSyncNotify); one getError call in each navigation runs 110–125ms
result.main_limitation: The bug gives no figure and the page JS is minified with URLs sanitised, so the profile cannot tell whether this busy period is the slowness the reporter means, or why the heap grows between navigations.
result.evidence:
Thread: t-3 GeckoMain, Isolated Web Content pid 3608, 22,725 samples over 45.8s (~2.0ms/sample), 12,814 non-idle (56%).

Episode windows (from the fmp start mark), active samples of total:
- 4.08–8.7s: 1769/2287. ScriptLoader 491, ModuleEvaluate 146, JS::Compile 101, indexedDB 210, PostMessageEvent 190, RunFrameRequestCallbacks 121, WaitForSyncNotify 122, Styles 98, DisplayList 86.
- 18.03–22.7s: 1909/2284. ScriptLoader 477, indexedDB 222, PostMessage 209, rAF 158, Incremental CC 114, Incremental GC 71, WaitForSyncNotify 124.
- 28.62–34.6s: 2115/2927. ScriptLoader 543, indexedDB 239, PostMessage 195, rAF 139, CC 116, GC 107, WaitForSyncNotify 130.
- Steady state 36–45.8s: 1943/4889 active. rAF 778, Incremental CC 330, Incremental GC 225, WaitForSyncNotify 116; ScriptLoader 0, indexedDB 15.

Milestones:
- FCP markers: 748ms, 743ms, 802ms.
- UserTiming browser-metric:tti: 1.515s, 1.223s, 1.393s.
- Longest LongTask per episode: m-33 423ms (5.904s), m-34 322ms (19.621s), m-35 270ms (31.577s).
- m-33 breakdown: 212 active samples, all under promise callback/AsyncFunctionNext page JS; GC/CC 58 (Major GC Mark 44); 5ms GCSlice markers back to back inside it.

GCMajor markers (reason, total_time, post_heap):
- 2.17s: CC_FINISHED, 79ms, 213MB
- 5.88s: TOO_MUCH_MALLOC, 133ms, 229MB
- 10.84s: CC_FINISHED, 162ms, 245MB
- 15.52s: CC_FINISHED, 167ms, 245MB
- 20.16s: TOO_MUCH_MALLOC, 206ms, 284MB
- 26.14s: CC_FINISHED, 322ms, 288MB
- 32.03s: CC_FINISHED, 362ms, max_pause 63.8ms, 325MB

CC markers: 134, 118, 300, 165, 337, 321, 639, 355, 412ms. mVisitedGCed 99,919 → 382,385 → 374,415 → 553,209 → 555,530 → 728,595. nsCycleCollector total 1030 samples.

Sync IPC:
- WaitForSyncNotify 739 samples; ZwWaitForAlertByThreadId self 813 (the top self frame, 6.3%). By sender: GetLinkResult 36.7%, GetError 31.6%, GetCompileResult ~9%, PBackgroundLSSnapshotConstructor 8.7%.
- Markers: PWebGL::Msg_GetError 303 calls (avg 1.69ms). The three largest, m-168 113ms @7.54s, m-169 111ms @21.13s and m-167 125ms @32.85s, sit under initWithImage ← initialiseTexture ← loadSpriteSheet.
- PWebGL::Msg_GetLinkResult: 47 calls (avg 12.7ms), firing about once per second for the whole capture, including steady state. Msg_GetCompileResult: 94 calls (avg 2.2ms).

Network: 724 requests from this thread, in flight 45% of the capture; the slowest is 1.55s.

DOMEvent: 1341 IndexedDB 'success' events (max 162ms); 278 'message' events (avg 7.3ms, max 110ms).
result.caveats:
- The bug states no figure, so I cannot confirm that the 4.6–6s post-navigation busy period is the slowness the reporter means. By the site's own metrics FCP is ~0.75s and TTI ~1.2–1.5s per navigation.
- That the three episodes are SPA route changes rather than full reloads is an inference: dynamic imports, no unload/DocumentLoad markers, same pid.
- The page JS is minified and URLs are sanitised, so I cannot name which app code allocates, or what drives the IndexedDB and postMessage traffic.
- I have not shown why the heap grows across navigations. It could be a page-side leak or retained state, or simply the app warming caches. A memory/allocation capture across repeated navigations would settle it.
- For the long GetError waits, the GPU-process side that services them is not in the capture: the threads filter excludes the canvas/WebGL thread, and the GPU GeckoMain and Renderer are idle during m-168. Why one GetError takes 110–125ms (for example, it flushing a pending texture upload) is a hypothesis, not observed.
- Sample counts come from substring searches and overlap; they are not exclusive buckets.
- One capture on one machine (i7-9750H). The steady-state rAF/GC activity is a resource-use concern rather than page load and is not analysed further.
